items: When you make an attack with a weapon made with a special material and you roll a 1, the weapon's resistance points are reduced by 1.
When you take a critical hit from an opponent, your armor's resistance points are reduced by 1.

entries: Each reduced point also reduces the attack bonus and damage for weapons, or the AC for armor, by 1.
A material that replaces another (for example, a coral armor replacing metal) uses the resistance values of the replaced material.

entries.name: Repairing Equipment
entries: To repair a piece of equipment made with a special material, you make a tools check using the required artisan tools. The DC equals 8 + total reduced points.
On a success, the equipment is fully repaired. On a failure, you can try again after a long rest.

entries.name: Common Items Resistance
entries: You can apply these rules to common materials like iron and wood. Determine resistance points using the market value of the items, and repair them with units of iron, wood, or other common materials.

craftingRule.name: Parts by Creature
entries: The following tables list example materials a character can harvest from creatures. They do not include weapons, armor, or gear the creature wears or carries. Every creature also has 1 unit of its creature type essence, extractable with an {@i essence extraction device}.

Some creatures list particular organs because they grant the creature special features (such as the essential organ that powers a dragon's breath weapon). See the {@variantrule Collecting Creature Parts|COMCRAF} rules for the number of harvest checks the characters can make per creature.

entries.caption: Aberrations and Oddities
rows: 1 brain; 4 hide; 1 mucous; 1 tail; 1d4 teeth; 3 tentacles

entries.caption: Beholders
rows: 1 central beholder eye; 2 small beholder eyes
1 central spectator eye; 1 small spectator eyes

entries.name: Dragons
entries: All dragons share the same base parts; the only differentiator is the dragon kin (black, blue, brass, bronze, copper, gold, green, red, silver, white). Feel free to add special or unique parts to each dragon type.

entries.caption: True Dragons (by Age)
rows: 4d4 claws; 1 essential organ; 2 horns; 8 scales; 4d4 teeth; 8 wings
4d4 claws; 1 essential organ; 2 horns; 6 scales; 4d4 teeth; 6 wings
1d4 claws; 1 essential organ; 2 horns; 4 scales; 2d4 teeth; 4 wings
2 claws; 1 essential organ; 2 horns; 2 scales; 1d4 teeth; 2 wings

entries.caption: Other Dragons and Draconic Creatures
rows: Same as adult dragon, but only 1d6 units of scales
Same as ancient dragon, but only 1d8 units of scales
Same as base dragon plus 1 shadow dragon dust; essential organ and scales (and other parts) become 'shadow dragon' variants

entries.caption: Elementals
rows: 1 mephit core (variants: dust, ice, magma, mud, smoke, steam)

entries.name: Giants
entries: All giants share the same base parts; the differentiator is the race (cloud, fire, frost, hill, stone, storm). Add special parts per race as desired.

entries.caption: Monstrosities
rows: 2 claws; 1 young red dragon essential organ; 1 young red dragon scales; 4 young red dragon wings
15 hide; 4 ink sac; 15 scales; 6d4 teeth; 2d4 tentacles

entries.name: Slaadi
entries: Note: a slaad only has a control gem if it was born from the Spawning Stone in Limbo.

entries.name: Reading Harvest Quantities
entries: Quantities like "2d4" or "1d6" indicate a die roll the DM uses to set the maximum number of units available from that part. The unit type (e.g., {@i hide}, {@i scales}, {@i venom sac}) is named on the part listing. All counts assume the maximum number of harvest checks for the creature's size; see the {@variantrule Collecting Creature Parts|COMCRAF} rules.

craftingRule.name: Plants and Herbs by Area
entries: When a character succeeds on a roll to gather plants and herbs, the DM can choose one of the following plants or roll a d20 to determine it randomly.

craftingRule.name: Scribing a Spell Scroll
entries: With time and patience, a spellcaster can transfer a spell to a scroll, creating a {@item spell scroll}.

entries.name: Resources
entries: Scribing a {@i spell scroll} takes an amount of time and money related to the level of the spell. The character must have proficiency in the {@skill Arcana} skill and must provide any material components required for the casting of the spell. The character must also have the spell prepared, or it must be among the character's known spells, in order to scribe a scroll of that spell.
If the scribed spell is a cantrip, the version of the scroll works as if the caster were 1st level.

craftingRule.name: Scribing Scroll Complications
entries: Crafting a {@i spell scroll} is a solitary task, unlikely to attract much attention. The complications that arise are more likely to involve the preparation needed for the activity. Every workweek spent scribing brings a 10 percent chance of a complication.

entries.caption: Scribe a Scroll Complications
rows: You bought up the last of the rare ink used to craft scrolls, angering a wizard in town.
The priest of a temple of good accuses you of trafficking in dark magic.*
A wizard eager to collect one of your spells in a book presses you to sell the scroll.
Due to a strange error in creating the scroll, it is instead a random spell of the same level.
The rare parchment you bought for your scrolls has a barely visible map on it.
A thief attempts to break into your workroom.*

entries.name: Recipe
entries: A successful Wisdom ({@skill Cooking|Arcadia11}) check grants a benefit to creatures who eat the prepared food. If the check succeeds by 5 or more, the recipe is delicious, granting an alternate benefit a creature may choose instead. If the {@dice d20} roll for the check is 20 and the check succeeds, the recipe is extra delicious, granting both previous benefits or a third alternative (as noted in the recipe).

craftingRule.name: Skill: Cooking
entries: {@b Wisdom (Cooking)} is the act of preparing, seasoning, and sautéing, baking, stewing, or otherwise turning harvested ingredients into food. Each recipe has its own DC for the Wisdom (Cooking) check required to make it based on its complexity.

craftingRule.name: Skill: Harvesting
entries: {@b Dexterity (Harvesting)} is the act of collecting usable ingredients, either from the earth or from a dead creature. The DC for harvesting usable ingredients from a dead creature is 10 + the creature's challenge rating.

entries.name: Recipe
entries: A successful Wisdom ({@skill Cooking|Arcadia11}) check grants a benefit to creatures who eat the prepared food. If the check succeeds by 5 or more, the recipe is delicious, granting an alternate benefit a creature may choose instead. If the {@dice d20} roll for the check is 20 and the check succeeds, the recipe is extra delicious, granting both previous benefits or a third alternative (as noted in the recipe).

craftingRule.name: Spellcasting with Monstrous Components
entries: When you cast a spell using a monstrous component, the new component replaces any material components normally required by the spell, except for components that have a cost of more than 300 gp.{@sup {@footnote 1|Game design note: many material components cost money, which requires adventuring. These components require dead monsters, which also requires adventuring, so that's why monster parts can replace some costly material components.}} These expensive material components must be provided as normal along with the monstrous component.

After you cast the spell, the monstrous component is consumed. A monstrous component can be used for a spell even if that spell doesn't typically require material components, or if the monstrous component doesn't replace any material components of the spell.
Monstrous components change a spell's effects as described below. Any effects of the spell that aren't noted remain the same. You can only use one monstrous component per casting of a spell.

The components in this article are organized by creature type. Creatures with an asterisk (*) next to their name can be found in {@loader Strongholds & Followers|collection/MCDM Productions; Strongholds and Followers.json}. Creatures with a dagger (†) can be found in {@loader Kingdoms & Warfare|book/MCDM Productions; Kingdoms & Warfare.json}.

craftingRule.name: Spells and Charges on Modular Items
entries: If an item has the charges or spell properties, the creator must decide which spell(s) to add when creating the item. The character must have proficiency in the {@skill Arcana} skill and provide any material components required for the casting of the spell. Moreover, the character must have the spell prepared, or it must be among the character's known spells.

For items with the Spell property, a character can choose only one spell. The spell level is determined by the property rarity. For example, an item with the Spell III property and the {@spell lightning bolt} spell casts it as a 7th-level spell.
For items with charges, a character can add multiple spells. The number of spells and maximum level depend on the rarity of the property.
Each charge equals 1 spell slot level. For example, expending 1 charge casts a 1st-level spell, and expending 5 charges casts a 5th-level spell.

craftingRule.name: The Twelve Uses of Dragon's Blood
entries: Every hedge-alchemist in Thelemar can tell you that dragon's blood is potent. Only a guild alchemist can tell you {@i how} — and even they will argue about it. What they agree on is the count: there are {@b twelve uses} of dragon's blood, and a thirteenth that nobody has written down and lived to publish.

Blood taken straight from the wyrm is powerful but narrow: it strengthens a spell of the dragon's own element, and nothing more (see {@item Dragon Blood (Wyrmling)|Ar8} and its kin). {@b Distillation} is what opens the rest. The process is neither quick nor forgiving, and it does not make the blood stronger — it makes it {@i broader}.

entries.name: Distilling
entries: Distilling one vial takes 8 hours of uninterrupted work, alchemist's supplies, and a successful check against the DC used to harvest the blood in the first place. A failed check ruins the vial; there is no partial result.
Distilled blood keeps indefinitely. It is the raw blood that spoils, which is why the guilds distil everything they can get and worry about buyers afterwards.

entries.name: Invoking a Use
entries: Distilled dragon's blood is a variant spell component. When you cast a spell using a vial, you choose which of the twelve uses to invoke. The vial is consumed either way.
How many you may invoke at once is a question of potency, not of skill — a wyrmling's blood will give up one use and no more, however good the alchemist.
No alchemist has drawn more than four uses from a single vial. Several have tried. The guild keeps their names on a plaque.

entries.name: The Twelve

items.name: 1. Far-Flung.
entries: Double the spell's range.

items.name: 2. Enduring.
entries: Double the spell's duration.

items.name: 3. Encompassing.
entries: Double the spell's area of effect.

items.name: 4. Manifold.
entries: Double the number of creatures the spell can target.

items.name: 5. Searing.
entries: Targets are vulnerable to the spell's damage type.

items.name: 6. Warding.
entries: If the spell grants resistance to a damage type, it grants immunity instead.

items.name: 7. Quickening.
entries: Cast the spell as a bonus action.

items.name: 8. Subtle.
entries: Cast the spell without verbal or somatic components.

items.name: 9. Piercing.
entries: Ignore resistance to the spell's damage type.

items.name: 10. Tenacious.
entries: The spell doesn't require {@status concentration}.

items.name: 11. Reliable.
entries: Treat any damage die that rolls a 1 or a 2 as a 3.

items.name: 12. Sanguine.
entries: The spell can't be counterspelled or dispelled.

{@note The same use can't be invoked twice on one casting, and two vials can't be combined — blood curdles against blood. Using more than one monstrous component on a casting still risks a wild magic surge as normal.}

craftingRule.name: Tinctures
entries: While herbs are certainly valuable in the powers they impart, a major hindrance to their usability is the lengthy preparations that some of them require. In these situations, it may be wise to brew that herb into a tincture. A tincture is the essence of an herb, distilled through various processes and designed to apply all the effects of a herb in a much faster time frame.

entries.name: Using a tincture
entries: Using a tincture takes an action and results in all the effects specified in the herb's description. Like herbs, a character may only benefit from the effects of one tincture or herb at a time. Using a new tincture while still under the effects of another tincture or herb, causes the first's effect to end immediately.

entries.name: Creating a tincture
entries: Creating a tincture is no easy feat, and requires intricate knowledge alchemy to perform successfully. In order to create a tincture, a character must possess proficiency in and have access to alchemy supplies. In addition, that character must expend an amount of money equal to double the base cost of the herb to buy ingredients and other materials. Creating a tincture requires one work week of labour to produce.
At the end of the process, the herb is destroyed and the character creates a tincture with the name '{@code tincture of [consumed herb]}'.

craftingRule.name: Variant Spell Components (Conversion Notes)
entries: Thelemar uses the variant spell components of {@i Arcadia} Issue 8 as its baseline. Arcadia 8 has precedence: where another source describes the same component, it may only {@i add} information (a price, a new spell it works with), never overwrite what Arcadia 8 already says.
The components below were reconciled from a supplementary table. Every deviation from that table is recorded here so the conversion stays auditable.

entries.name: Added to Arcadia 8 (prices only)
entries: Arcadia 8 lists no gold values. Four were merged in without touching any effect text: {@item Ettercap Foot|Ar8} 200 gp, {@item Unicorn Blood|Ar8} 350 gp, {@item Troll Blood|Ar8} 2,000 gp, and {@item Unicorn Horn|Ar8} 2,800 gp.

entries.name: Renamed or reinterpreted
entries: {@b Marilith Blade Shard} names a table row whose component name had been truncated to a single letter. The effect (striking the same target more than once with {@spell steel wind strike|XGE}) matches a marilith's six blades, and follows the naming of Arcadia 8's own {@item Erinyes Longsword Shards|Ar8}.
{@b Mirage Arcane} — the table read "Arcane MIrage", which is {@spell mirage arcane} with its words reversed.
{@b Distilled Dragon's Blood} — see below.

The table writes component names with possessives ({@i Glabrezu's Horn}) where Arcadia 8 does not ({@i Glabrezu Horn}), and inverts word order ({@i Mindkiller's Piece of Brain} against {@i Piece of Mindkiller Brain}). These are the same components, not new ones.

entries.name: Distilled Dragon's Blood, and the Twelve Uses
entries: The supplementary table gave dragon's blood the power to double a spell's range, duration, area {@i and} targets while making its targets vulnerable to its damage type, all at once, for a flat 10,000 gp. That is four metamagics and doubled damage on a single consumable.

Thelemar instead follows the alchemical tradition of {@variantrule The Twelve Uses of Dragon's Blood|TGTT}, which is now the canonical rule. Arcadia 8's raw {@item Dragon Blood (Wyrmling)|Ar8} and its kin are preserved unchanged — they remain the narrow, undistilled form — and Arcadia 8's {@item Dragon Blood (Protection)|Ar8} appears among the twelve as {@i Warding}.

entries.name: Dropped
entries: Six rows carrying a component name but neither a spell nor an effect (a spreadsheet fill-down), and one row duplicated verbatim.

itemMaterial.name: Adamant

effects.note: Nearly indestructible.

entries: Adamant is extremely heavy, nearly indestructible, and strongly receptive to magic.

itemMaterial.name: Adamantine

effects.note: Cannot be destroyed, damaged or worn down except by extraordinarily powerful magic or natural phenomena.

entries: An ultra-hard alloy of adamant, mithril, and electrum. Adamantine is deep blue with a metallic tinge that sharpens to purple-white under light from most magical sources.

items: Adamantine Heavy Armor reduces incoming Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage by 3; Medium Armor reduces it by 2.
An adamantine shield grants +2 additional AC.
Adamantine equipment cannot be destroyed, damaged, or worn down except by extraordinarily powerful magic or natural phenomena.

itemMaterial.name: Ashglass

effects.text: Ashglass can extinguish a nonmagical flame no larger than a 5-foot Cube by touch. When its user takes fire damage, they can take a Reaction to gain Resistance to that instance of damage; the glass then becomes inert until the next Long Rest.

effects.name: Ashglass Ward
effects.note: When you take fire damage, gain Resistance to that instance of damage. The glass then becomes inert until the next Long Rest.

effects.text: Water suppresses its affinity for 1 hour.

entries: {@b Affinity.} Ashglass can extinguish a nonmagical flame no larger than a 5-foot Cube by touch. When its user takes Fire damage, they can take a Reaction to gain Resistance to that instance of damage; the glass then becomes inert until the next Long Rest.
{@b Instability.} Water suppresses its affinity for 1 hour.

itemMaterial.name: Bone and Horn
entries: Bone and horn can form rigid armor plates, hafts, bows, needles, and simple weapon edges.

itemMaterial.name: Brass
entries: Brass is an alloy of copper and zinc used for fittings, instruments, vessels, and mechanisms. It is too soft for durable weapon edges.

itemMaterial.name: Bronze
entries: Bronze is an alloy of copper and tin used for weapons, armor, bells, statuary, and fittings. It is easier to cast than steel but does not keep as hard an edge.

itemMaterial.name: Cloudpearl

effects.text: A creature that spends Hit Dice during a Short Rest while holding Cloudpearl regains additional Hit Points equal to its Proficiency Bonus.
Cold damage suppresses this benefit until the pearl spends 1 minute in a fire or another source of strong heat.

entries: {@b Affinity.} A creature that spends Hit Dice during a Short Rest while holding Cloudpearl regains additional Hit Points equal to its Proficiency Bonus.
{@b Instability.} Cold damage suppresses this benefit until the pearl spends 1 minute in a fire or another source of strong heat.

itemMaterial.name: Cold Iron

effects.note: Deals an additional weapon damage die against fey creatures.

entries: A rare pure-formed iron, mined deep underground and forged at lower temperatures to preserve its delicate properties.

items: Weapons made of cold iron deal an additional weapon damage die against fey creatures

itemMaterial.name: Common Cloth
entries: Linen, wool, hemp, and cotton are used for clothing, padding, sails, and soft containers. Cloth cannot form a weapon's striking surface or rigid armor by itself.

itemMaterial.name: Common Wood
entries: Common woods such as ash, oak, yew, and beech are used for hafts, bows, shields, and tools. The species and seasoning affect the finished item, but common wood has no special material rules.

itemMaterial.name: Copper
entries: Copper is soft, workable, and widely used for coins, vessels, fittings, and wiring.

itemMaterial.name: Darkeline

effects.conditional: On checks and saving throws made to resist being moved against your will

entries: Darkeline is starmetal-alloyed Darkmetal. It feels no heavier than steel at rest but becomes massively dense at the instant of impact. A Darkeline weapon gains Heavy and cannot have Light or Finesse. A creature wearing Darkeline armor has Advantage on checks and saving throws made to resist being moved against its will, but its Speed is reduced by 5 feet.

itemMaterial.name: Darkmetal
entries: Darkmetal is hard and unusually heavy.

items: Armor made from darkmetal is Heavy Armor, imposes Disadvantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks, and increases its Strength requirement by 2. If the armor normally adds a Dexterity modifier to AC, reduce that modifier by 1.
A darkmetal shield grants 1 more AC than an ordinary shield of its type.
A darkmetal weapon gains the Heavy property and loses the Light and Finesse properties.

itemMaterial.name: Darkwood (Zalantar)
entries: This rare magical wood has similar properties to beech, oak and yew for bow-making while being extremely light and durable.

items: Items made of darkwood lose the Heavy property.

itemMaterial.name: Deathglass

effects.text: When a living creature dies within 10 feet, Deathglass can hold one death charge for 24 hours. A weapon or focus made from it can expend that charge to deal an extra {@damage 2d6} necrotic damage to one target damaged by it.

effects.name: Deathglass Charge
effects.note: Expend a stored death charge to deal an extra {@damage 2d6} necrotic damage to one target damaged by this item. A charge is held for 24 hours when a living creature dies within 10 feet.

effects.text: If the charge expires, its bearer takes {@damage 2d6} necrotic damage.

entries: {@b Affinity.} When a living creature dies within 10 feet, Deathglass can hold one death charge for 24 hours. A weapon or focus made from it can expend that charge to deal an extra 2d6 Necrotic damage to one target damaged by it.
{@b Instability.} If the charge expires, its bearer takes 2d6 Necrotic damage.

itemMaterial.name: Deep Crystal

magicCapacityRules.note: When an enchantment is first placed on deep crystal, its maker immediately knows whether another effect in the object would interfere with it, before committing the materials.

effects.note: A weapon with a deep-crystal striking surface can be used as a spellcasting focus.

entries: Deep crystal forms at the heart of large mineral veins and is renowned for its strength and magical resonance. A weapon with a deep-crystal striking surface can be used as a spellcasting focus. When an enchantment is first placed on deep crystal, its maker immediately knows whether another effect in the object would interfere with it, before committing the materials.

itemMaterial.name: Desert Ironwood

effects.note: Increased normal range equal to half its current normal range.

entries: A tree with a thin trunk and many narrow branches, desert ironwood is both dense and strong. Because they only flower and fruit four years per decade, desert ironwood is scarce, but where one tree is found, there are others nearby. These trees, which thrive anywhere from lush oases to barren deserts, provide the ecosystem with shade and food, granting all manner of desert creatures refuge within the canopies. Because desert ironwood twists and knots as it grows, finding a tree with a suitable piece of wood is a challenge, and only advanced masterwork artisans can work with this dense, unyielding wood. Desert ironwood is dark, with reddish hues and violet striations throughout. Its density makes it durable, though quite heavy; items made of it are 25 percent heavier than their mundane counterparts.

items: A ranged weapon made from desert ironwood has an increased normal range equal to half of its current normal range. For instance, a shortbow made of desert iron wood has a normal range of 120 feet and a long range of 480 feet.
Weapon attacks made with a melee weapon made of desert ironwood score a critical hit on a roll of 19 or 20.

itemMaterial.name: Dragon Bone

effects.text: Structures reinforced with dragon bone have Resistance to all damage from nonmagical impacts.

entries: Dragon bones are sturdy yet supple, extraordinarily light, and able to withstand tremendous force without breaking or deteriorating. Dragon-bone equipment weighs half as much as an ordinary equivalent. Weapons made from it lose the Heavy property, and structures reinforced with it have Resistance to all damage from nonmagical impacts. The bones are sought after for armor, siegecraft, and monuments intended to survive an age.

itemMaterial.name: Dragon Heart

effects.text: A properly housed dragon heart can power a magical construct indefinitely, or replace material components worth up to 10,000 gp in a resurrection spell, after which it stops.

entries: A dragon's heart often continues beating after death. Properly housed, it can power a magical construct indefinitely or replace material components worth up to 10,000 gp in a resurrection spell, after which it stops. Fear Dragon hearts beat in erratic, disturbing rhythms and can power effects based on coercion, destruction, or fear. Safety Dragon hearts maintain perfect, soothing patterns and can power wards, healing, or protective constructs. A heart is a unique organ, never a bulk commodity.

itemMaterial.name: Dragon Scales
entries: Dragon scales are hard plates used for armor, shields, and weapon reinforcement.

{@b Equipment.} A shield reinforced primarily with Dragon Scales grants 1 additional AC. Other equipment uses the material properties above regardless of the kind of dragon from which the scales came.
{@b Domain Resonance.} A Dragon Scale item may carry one Draconic Domain Resonance from its source dragon.

itemMaterial.name: Dragon Teeth and Claws
entries: Dragon teeth and claws retain an edge with little shaping.
{@b Equipment.} Teeth are commonly used for piercing weapons, while claws are used for slashing weapons and hooked tools. Both use the material properties above.
{@b Domain Resonance.} An item made from a Dragon Tooth or Claw may carry one Draconic Domain Resonance from its source dragon.

itemMaterial.name: Dragonhide
entries: Dragonhide is cut from the supple portions beneath and between a dragon's scales.
{@b Equipment.} Properly cured Dragonhide can form Light, Medium, or Heavy Armor. It uses the material properties above regardless of the kind of dragon from which it came.
{@b Domain Resonance.} A Dragonhide item may carry one Draconic Domain Resonance from its source dragon.

itemMaterial.name: Duststone

degradation.note: Its Damage decreases by 1 until rebuilt during a Short Rest with mason's tools.

effects.text: A Duststone weapon deals double damage to nonmagical objects and structures.
On a natural 1 attack roll, its Damage decreases by 1 until rebuilt during a Short Rest with mason's tools.

entries: {@b Affinity.} A Duststone weapon deals double damage to nonmagical objects and structures.
{@b Instability.} On a natural 1 attack roll, its Damage decreases by 1 until rebuilt during a Short Rest with mason's tools.

itemMaterial.name: Electrum

magicCapacityRules.note: Two opposed states of one magical property, such as revealing and concealing or heating and cooling, count as one effect when only one state can function at a time.

entries: Electrum is a naturally occurring or deliberately made alloy of gold and silver. It is valued for enchantments concerned with exchange, duality, and transformation. Two opposed states of one magical property, such as revealing and concealing or heating and cooling, count as one effect against an electrum item's Magic Capacity when only one state can function at a time.

itemMaterial.name: Emberglass

effects.text: Emberglass is warm even in winter and kindles dry material touched to it for a minute. A weapon made from it can deal fire damage instead of its normal type.
Cold damage or immersion in water suppresses its affinity until the end of the user's next turn.

entries: {@b Affinity.} Emberglass is warm even in winter and kindles dry material touched to it for a minute. A weapon made from it can deal Fire damage instead of its normal type.
{@b Instability.} Cold damage or immersion in water suppresses its affinity until the end of the user's next turn.

itemMaterial.name: Gold
entries: Gold is heavy, soft, and poor at holding an edge. Gold equipment is usually ceremonial or built around a harder core, and its main value is as a conduit for enchantments.

itemMaterial.name: Goldleaf Wood

effects.text: An object convincingly made from goldleaf requires a successful {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) check to distinguish from gold by sight alone, though its weight reveals the difference immediately.

entries: Goldleaf wood resembles polished gold and is used for instruments, carving, and ceremonial fittings. An object convincingly made from Goldleaf requires a successful DC 15 Intelligence (Investigation) check to distinguish from gold by sight alone, though its weight reveals the difference immediately.

itemMaterial.name: Gravesalt

effects.text: An intact Gravesalt container preserves nonliving organic material indefinitely. A creature hit by a Gravesalt weapon cannot regain Hit Points until the start of the user's next turn.
Fresh water dissolves exposed Gravesalt in 1 minute.

entries: {@b Affinity.} An intact Gravesalt container preserves nonliving organic material indefinitely. A creature hit by a Gravesalt weapon cannot regain Hit Points until the start of the user's next turn.
{@b Instability.} Fresh water dissolves exposed Gravesalt in 1 minute.

itemMaterial.name: Heart Stone

effects.note: Untouched by time and the strife of the world.

effects.text: Heart Stone makes no noise when something strikes it. The craft of making it was lost in The Collapse; no new Heart Stone has been worked since.

entries: Heart Stone is often a white, somewhat warm to the touch material. It has a smooth texture and is of moderate weight, and makes no noise when something hits it.

One of the {@b Empire's} earliest and most defining inventions, Heart Stone is believed to have been a leading cause of its rise to dominance, and the craft of making it was {@b lost in The Collapse} - no new Heart Stone has been worked since. It is untouched by time and the strife of the world, which is why its greatest works still stand: above all the {@b Flard}, the oracle pillars, alongside other Imperial relics such as the Starlight Roads and the towering Great Statues.

itemMaterial.name: Ioun Crystal

magicCapacityRules.note: An Ioun fragment can serve as a spellcasting focus for one effect aligned with its resonance; that effect does not count against the fragment's Magic Capacity.

entries: Ioun Crystal is a natural conduit to the Positive Energy Plane. It forms inside geodes near the boundary of the Quasi-Elemental Plane of Mineral. Whole crystals are called {@b Ioun Stones}; broken pieces are {@b Ioun fragments}; the crystalline web around them is {@b Ioun Sand}.

{@b Ioun Fragments.} A fragment retains the resonance of the stone from which it broke but not that stone's complete property. It can serve as a spellcasting focus for one effect aligned with that resonance; the aligned effect does not count against the fragment's Magic Capacity. Unlike Jadoo, it cannot hold unrelated magic without limit.

{@b Ioun Geodes.} An intact Ioun geode is an unattractive shell about 1 foot across, though some grow much larger. It contains {@dice 3d4} Ioun Stones suspended in a crystalline web and surrounded by Ioun Sand. Breaking it releases centuries of trapped Positive Energy: each creature within 30 feet must make a {@dc 20} Constitution saving throw, taking {@damage 6d12 + 8} Radiant damage on a failed save or half as much on a successful one. Creatures native to the Mineral Plane often cultivate geodes and consider their removal theft.

itemMaterial.name: Ioun Sand

effects.note: Each coherent numerical property granted by an intact Ioun Stone set in the matrix is doubled, including bonuses, ranges, areas, damage, healing, capacities and durations. Ioun Sand does not double ordinary enchantments, Dragon Blood uses, or the effects of loose Ioun fragments.

entries: Ioun Sand is the heavy, glittering crystalline web that surrounds stones inside an intact geode. A master jeweler and spellcaster can shape it into a matrix such as a helm, bracer, staff, halo, pendant, or torc. An actual Ioun Stone placed in the matrix remains until deliberately removed, and each coherent numerical property granted by that stone is doubled, including bonuses, ranges, areas, damage, healing, capacities, and durations. The DM adjudicates properties that cannot coherently be doubled.

Ioun Sand does not double ordinary enchantments, Dragon Blood uses, or the effects of loose Ioun fragments. Complete matrices holding several intact stones are among the rarest magical devices in existence.

itemMaterial.name: Iron
entries: Iron is a common material for tools, weapons, armor, and fittings. It rusts unless maintained or protected.

itemMaterial.name: Ironwood

effects.text: Ironwood is as strong, heavy and fire-resistant as steel, and will not burn.
Spells and effects that affect metal do not affect ironwood; spells that affect wood do.

entries: Ironwood is a magical substance created from normal wood by druids, mimicking the properties of Desert Ironwood.

items: While remaining natural wood in almost every way, ironwood is as strong, heavy, and resistant to fire as steel.
Spells and effects that affect metal do not affect ironwood, whereas spells that affect wood do - although ironwood will not burn.

itemMaterial.name: Ivory
entries: Ivory is dense, fine-grained, and used for carving, inlays, holy symbols, and wand components.

itemMaterial.name: Jadoo

effects.text: A creature touching an unshielded piece of Jadoo for the first time must succeed on a {@dc 13} Constitution saving throw or be {@condition incapacitated} until the start of its next turn.

entries: A rare crystal found in the Black Desert and, unbeknownst to most scholars, within the Starlight Roads, Jadoo is coveted as a raw form of magic. It can host any number of unrelated magical effects without interference and was used in modern attempts to reproduce Maathaum and Sumaathaum. Bare contact creates a moment of sensory overload: Jadoo is described as tasting of every taste, smelling of every scent, and sounding like all melodies at once. A creature touching an unshielded piece for the first time must succeed on a DC 13 Constitution saving throw or be Incapacitated until the start of its next turn.

itemMaterial.name: Lead

effects.conditional: Against Abjuration, Divination, Enchantment and Illusion spells

effects.text: A sufficiently thick lead enclosure blocks divination magic through it.
Lead cannot hold any magical effects.

entries: Lead blocks magic. Lead-coated armor grants Advantage on saving throws against Abjuration, Divination, Enchantment, and Illusion spells, while a sufficiently thick enclosure blocks divination magic through it.
Lead cannot hold any magical effects.

itemMaterial.name: Leather and Rawhide
entries: Leather and rawhide are used for flexible armor, straps, sheaths, and protective clothing. Untreated pieces are vulnerable to water, rot, and fire.

itemMaterial.name: Lifeglass

effects.text: When a spell cast through Lifeglass restores Hit Points, one healing die that rolled a 1 or 2 can be rerolled.
If the target is already at its Hit Point maximum, it instead takes radiant damage equal to the spell's level.

entries: {@b Affinity.} When a spell cast through Lifeglass restores Hit Points, one healing die that rolled a 1 or 2 can be rerolled.
{@b Instability.} If the target is already at its Hit Point maximum, it instead takes Radiant damage equal to the spell's level.

itemMaterial.name: Magmaheart

effects.text: After a Magmaheart weapon hits a creature wearing manufactured armor, the next attack against that creature before the start of the user's next turn gains a +1 bonus.
Cold damage makes it contract explosively, dealing {@damage 1d6} force damage to the creature carrying it.

instability.note: Cold damage makes it contract explosively, dealing {@damage 1d6} force damage to the creature carrying it.

entries: {@b Affinity.} After a Magmaheart weapon hits a creature wearing manufactured armor, the next attack against that creature before the start of the user's next turn gains a +1 bonus.
{@b Instability.} Cold damage makes it contract explosively, dealing 1d6 Force damage to the creature carrying it.

itemMaterial.name: Mercurial Steel

effects.text: When forged, choose two weapon or tool configurations that use roughly the same amount of material. As a Bonus Action, the user can shift the item between those forms.

The metal closes minor dents and cracks during a Long Rest. Antimagic locks it in its current form, and a critical hit against an unattended Mercurial Steel object ruptures it, exposing nearby creatures to Quicksilver.

entries: Mercurial Steel encloses quicksilver channels within a flexible steel lattice. When forged, choose two weapon or tool configurations that use roughly the same amount of material. As a Bonus Action, its user can shift the item between those forms. The metal closes minor dents and cracks during a Long Rest. Antimagic locks it in its current form, and a critical hit against an unattended Mercurial Steel object ruptures it, exposing nearby creatures to Quicksilver.

itemMaterial.name: Mineralite

effects.text: Once per day, touching Mineralite to a damaged nonmagical object for 1 minute repairs a break or tear no larger than 1 foot in any dimension.

effects.name: Mineralite Mending
effects.note: Once per day, touch Mineralite to a damaged nonmagical object for 1 minute to repair a break or tear no larger than 1 foot in any dimension.

effects.text: Magical interference doubles the item's weight until one of its magical effects is removed.

entries: {@b Affinity.} Once per day, touching Mineralite to a damaged nonmagical object for 1 minute repairs a break or tear no larger than 1 foot in any dimension.
{@b Instability.} Magical interference doubles the item's weight until one of its magical effects is removed.

itemMaterial.name: Mirror Amalgam

effects.note: Once per Long Rest when a Divination or Illusion spell is cast through it, the caster can double either the spell's range or its duration.

effects.text: Fire damage that reaches the coating destroys it.

entries: Mirror Amalgam is a sealed silver-and-quicksilver coating applied to glass, crystal, or polished obsidian. It can serve as a focus for Divination and Illusion spells. Once per Long Rest when such a spell is cast through it, the caster can double either the spell's range or its duration. Fire damage that reaches the coating destroys it. A mirror used repeatedly to contact spirits can also become contaminated, replaying images supplied by the spirit rather than true reflections.

itemMaterial.name: Mithraline

effects.note: Gains Versatile if appropriate, and gains Finesse.

entries: Mithraline is a starmetal alloy that intensifies Mithril's lightness and magical flexibility. Equipment made from it weighs one quarter as much as normal. Armor has no Strength requirement, imposes no Disadvantage on Dexterity (Stealth), and can be concealed beneath clothing. Weapons lose Heavy and Two-Handed, gain Versatile if appropriate, and gain Finesse. Its pale surface bends around enchantments rather than resisting them, accounting for its exceptional Magic Capacity.

itemMaterial.name: Mithril
entries: Mithril is extraordinarily light and flexible without becoming soft.

items: Mithril armor imposes no Disadvantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks, has no Strength requirement, and can be concealed beneath ordinary clothing if its shape permits.
A mithril weapon loses the Heavy property. A Two-Handed weapon becomes Versatile, a one-handed weapon without Light gains Light, and a Light weapon gains Finesse.

itemMaterial.name: Nightsilk

effects.note: Creatures take a −2 penalty to Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) checks based on sight made to notice the wearer of an outer garment made primarily from Nightsilk.

entries: A type of silk produced by purple-spotted caterpillars from the Ossmark Forest of Clairnia. Its folds drift slowly even in still air, creating a blur around the wearer without hindering movement.
While wearing an outer garment made primarily from Nightsilk, creatures take a -2 penalty to Wisdom (Perception) checks based on sight made to notice the wearer.

itemMaterial.name: Obsidian

degradation.note: The edge shatters and its Damage decreases by 2 until it is re-knapped during a Short Rest with appropriate tools.

entries: Freshly knapped obsidian takes a sharp but brittle edge. When its wielder rolls a natural 1 on an attack roll, the edge shatters and its Damage decreases by 2 until it is re-knapped during a Short Rest with appropriate tools. Polished obsidian also has arcane uses.

itemMaterial.name: Ordinary Glass

degradation.note: A glass weapon shatters after it scores a critical hit or when its wielder rolls a natural 1 on an attack roll.

entries: Ordinary glass is used for lenses, vessels, alchemical equipment, and cutting edges. It is too brittle for protective equipment. A glass weapon shatters after it scores a critical hit or when its wielder rolls a natural 1 on an attack roll.

itemMaterial.name: Orichalcum

effects.text: Orichalcum cannot safely store enchantments.

entries: Orichalcum is light, hard, keen, and disruptive to magic.

items: Orichalcum armor imposes no Disadvantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks and has no Strength requirement.
An orichalcum weapon counts as magical for the purpose of overcoming resistance and immunity.
Orichalcum cannot safely store enchantments.

itemMaterial.name: Orichaline

effects.note: Ignores AC bonuses granted by spells or other temporary magical effects when determining whether a miss becomes a Penetrating Blow. It cannot bypass physical armor, cover, or a creature's natural defenses in this way.

entries: Orichaline is starmetal-alloyed Orichalcum, dark green and traced with bright lines around active magic. An Orichaline weapon counts as magical and ignores AC bonuses granted by spells or other temporary magical effects when determining whether a miss becomes a Penetrating Blow. It cannot bypass physical armor, cover, or a creature's natural defenses in this way.

itemMaterial.name: Paradox Metal

effects.text: Paradox Metal cannot be magically tracked, and can host souls in a unique fashion — protecting them from detection and exorcism, but also preventing them from escaping its confines.

entries: An alloy of darkmetal and mithril, rumored to only be craftable in planes where magic is highly suffused, such as the feywild. This metal can store enormous amounts of magic in it, and cannot be magically tracked. It can host souls in a very unique fashion, protecting them from detection and exorcism but also preventing them from escaping its confines.

itemMaterial.name: Platinum
entries: Platinum is dense, difficult to work, and resistant to corrosion.

itemMaterial.name: Quicksilver

effects.text: Quicksilver cannot form equipment by itself. A creature exposed to an open vial or ruptured channel must succeed on a {@dc 14} Constitution saving throw or take {@damage 2d6} poison damage and have the {@condition poisoned} condition for 1 hour.

entries: Quicksilver is a toxic liquid metal used in alchemy, sealed mechanisms, and amalgams. It cannot form equipment by itself. A creature exposed to an open vial or ruptured channel must succeed on a DC 14 Constitution saving throw or take 2d6 Poison damage and have the Poisoned condition for 1 hour.

itemMaterial.name: Rimeglass

degradation.note: Fire damage reduces its Protection and Critical to 0 until it is repaired during a Short Rest with smith's or glassblower's tools.

effects.text: A creature critically hit by a Rimeglass weapon has its Speed reduced by 10 feet until the end of its next turn.
Fire damage reduces its Protection and Critical to 0 until it is repaired during a Short Rest with smith's or glassblower's tools.

entries: {@b Affinity.} A creature critically hit by a Rimeglass weapon has its Speed reduced by 10 feet until the end of its next turn.
{@b Instability.} Fire damage reduces its Protection and Critical to 0 until it is repaired during a Short Rest with smith's or glassblower's tools.

itemMaterial.name: Rootstone

effects.text: While its user stands on earth or stone, they have Advantage on checks and saving throws made to resist being shoved or knocked {@condition prone}.

effects.conditional: While standing on earth or stone, to resist being shoved or knocked prone

effects.text: Armor made from Rootstone reduces its wearer's Speed by 5 feet.

entries: {@b Affinity.} While its user stands on earth or stone, they have Advantage on checks and saving throws made to resist being shoved or knocked Prone.
{@b Instability.} Armor made from Rootstone reduces its wearer's Speed by 5 feet.

itemMaterial.name: Rose Gold

magicCapacityRules.theme: loyalty, affection, status and public identity
magicCapacityRules.note: The first such effect placed on an item does not count against its Magic Capacity.

entries: This alloy of gold and traces of Mithril is expensive but common among high-end smiths. It counters gold's softness and makes luxury weapons and armor viable for real combat. Rose Gold readily carries magic concerned with loyalty, affection, status, and public identity; the first such effect placed on an item does not count against its Magic Capacity.

itemMaterial.name: Shell and Chitin
entries: Large shells and monster chitin can be fitted into shields and Light or Medium Armor. They require a carver rather than a smith to work and repair.

itemMaterial.name: Silk
entries: Silk is light, strong for its weight, and commonly used for fine clothing and rope.

itemMaterial.name: Silver

effects.note: Bypasses Resistance or Immunity to mundane weapons only when the creature's rules specifically say silver does so.

entries: Some creatures, including many werewolves, can be harmed normally by silvered weapons even when ordinary weapons fail. A properly silvered weapon bypasses Resistance or Immunity to mundane weapons only when the creature's rules specifically say that silver does so.

itemMaterial.name: Skyshard

effects.text: Equipment made primarily from Skyshard weighs one quarter as much, and a Skyshard weapon's normal and long thrown ranges increase by 20 feet.
When it takes thunder damage, a creature holding or wearing it must succeed on a {@dc 13} Strength saving throw or be pushed 10 feet.

instability.note: When it takes thunder damage, a creature holding or wearing it must succeed on a {@dc 13} Strength saving throw or be pushed 10 feet.

entries: {@b Affinity.} Equipment made primarily from Skyshard weighs one quarter as much, and a Skyshard weapon's normal and long thrown ranges increase by 20 feet.
{@b Instability.} When it takes Thunder damage, a creature holding or wearing it must succeed on a DC 13 Strength saving throw or be pushed 10 feet.

itemMaterial.name: Smokestone

effects.text: As a Bonus Action, its user can create a 10-foot-radius Sphere of smoke that is Heavily Obscured for 1 minute or until dispersed by a strong wind.

effects.name: Smokestone Cloud
effects.note: Create a 10-foot-radius Sphere of heavily obscuring smoke for 1 minute.

effects.text: Creatures relying on smell have Advantage on checks made to locate its carrier.

entries: {@b Affinity.} As a Bonus Action, its user can create a 10-foot-radius Sphere of smoke that is Heavily Obscured for 1 minute or until dispersed by a strong wind.
{@b Instability.} Creatures relying on smell have Advantage on checks made to locate its carrier.

itemMaterial.name: Starmetal

effects.text: Starmetal has few useful properties by itself, but produces unusual effects when alloyed — see Mithraline, Orichaline, Darkeline and Steeline.

entries: Starmetal has few useful properties by itself but produces unusual effects when alloyed with other metals.

itemMaterial.name: Steel
entries: Steel is the standard material for modern weapons and armor. It is harder and more resilient than wrought iron.

itemMaterial.name: Steeline

magicCapacityRules.note: Two effects above its Magic Capacity are required before the interference DC increases by 1.

entries: This deep red alloy of iron and starmetal is found only where a meteor struck an iron deposit and the metals fused under impossible pressure. Modern smiths can rework it but cannot reproduce it. Steeline holds enchantments in isolated crystalline channels; if it ever becomes overloaded, two effects above its Magic Capacity are required before the interference DC increases by 1.

itemMaterial.name: Stone and Flint

degradation.note: Its striking edge chips and its Damage decreases by 1 additional step until repaired or replaced.

entries: Knapped flint and shaped stone can form sharp but fragile tools and weapon edges. They cannot be used for flexible weapons or working mechanisms. When the wielder rolls a natural 1 on an attack roll with a stone weapon, its striking edge chips and its Damage decreases by 1 additional step until repaired or replaced.

itemMaterial.name: Stormprism

effects.text: Its user gains a +1 bonus to Initiative and can take a Reaction immediately after being hit to move up to 10 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks.

effects.name: Stormprism Surge
effects.note: Immediately after being hit, move up to 10 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks.

effects.text: On a natural 1 involving the item, its user takes {@damage 1d6} lightning damage.

instability.note: On a natural 1 involving the item, its user takes {@damage 1d6} lightning damage.

entries: {@b Affinity.} Its user gains a +1 bonus to Initiative and can take a Reaction immediately after being hit to move up to 10 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks.
{@b Instability.} On a natural 1 involving the item, its user takes 1d6 Lightning damage.

itemMaterial.name: Stout Blackwood

effects.note: On a critical hit with a ranged stout blackwood weapon that has the loading property.

effects.name: Stout Blackwood Shove
effects.note: Once per turn when you hit with a two-handed stout blackwood melee weapon, contest Strength (Athletics) against the target's Athletics or Acrobatics; on a success, knock it prone or push it 5 feet.

entries: Characterized by their ability to survive in the harshest weather, stout blackwood trees are found in remote locations throughout mountainous regions. Stout blackwoods have thinner trunks, heavily ringed with the passing of short, rough growing seasons. They tend to grow in abundance in valleys where snow and rain collect or near glacier-fed rivers. Their leaves are tiny and needle-like, staying on year-round to gather whatever bits of sunlight filter through the cloudy, snowy days. In the first weeks of warmer weather, stout blackwoods flower and fruit, attracting creatures emerging from hibernation. While the bark of stout blackwood trees is white, the wood inside is a rich black. These trees produce stiff, sturdy wood that creates extreme tension in ranged weapons; stout blackwood shortbows and longbows are hard to use, but crossbows made of it are granted heightened accuracy and impact. This wood also absorbs the force of impact, which makes it particularly useful in crafting melee weapons. Stout blackwood is a superb material for masterwork artisans ranging in skill from beginner to advanced.

items: When you score a critical hit using a ranged weapon made from stout blackwood that has the loading property, you deal an extra 1d4 damage of the weapon's type.

Once per turn when you hit a creature using a two-handed melee weapon made from stout blackwood, you can make a Strength (Athletics) check contested by the target's Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics) check (the target chooses the ability to use). If you succeed, you either knock the target prone or push them 5 feet away from you (your choice).

itemMaterial.name: Sunprism

effects.text: Sunprism sheds bright light in a 20-foot radius and dim light for a further 20 feet on command. As a Magic action, its user can outline {@condition invisible} creatures and objects in the bright light until the start of the user's next turn.

effects.name: Sunprism Outline
effects.note: Outline {@condition invisible} creatures and objects in the bright light until the start of your next turn.

effects.text: Magical Darkness of spell level 3 or higher suppresses it while their areas overlap.

entries: {@b Affinity.} Sunprism sheds bright light in a 20-foot radius and dim light for a further 20 feet on command. As a Magic action, its user can outline Invisible creatures and objects in the bright light until the start of the user's next turn.
{@b Instability.} Magical Darkness of spell level 3 or higher suppresses it while their areas overlap.

itemMaterial.name: Tideglass

effects.text: When an attack hits its wearer, the wearer can take a Reaction to move 5 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks.

effects.name: Tideglass Slip
effects.note: When an attack hits you, move 5 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks.

effects.text: Cold damage suppresses this movement until the end of the wearer's next turn.

entries: {@b Affinity.} When an attack hits its wearer, the wearer can take a Reaction to move 5 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks.
{@b Instability.} Cold damage suppresses this movement until the end of the wearer's next turn.

itemMaterial.name: Vitriol Crystal

effects.text: Vitriol Crystal repairs its own mundane damage during a Long Rest. A weapon made from it can deal acid damage instead of its normal type.
On a natural 1 attack roll, its user takes {@damage 1d4} acid damage.

instability.note: On a natural 1 attack roll, its user takes {@damage 1d4} acid damage.

entries: {@b Affinity.} Vitriol Crystal repairs its own mundane damage during a Long Rest. A weapon made from it can deal Acid damage instead of its normal type.
{@b Instability.} On a natural 1 attack roll, its user takes 1d4 Acid damage.

itemMaterial.name: Voidglass

effects.text: On command, a Voidglass item produces no sound and grants Advantage on Dexterity ({@skill Stealth}) checks that depend on moving quietly.

effects.conditional: on checks that depend on moving quietly
effects.note: On command, a Voidglass item produces no sound.

effects.text: While this property is active, its user cannot speak or provide Verbal spell components.

entries: {@b Affinity.} On command, a Voidglass item produces no sound and grants Advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks that depend on moving quietly.
{@b Instability.} While this property is active, its user cannot speak or provide Verbal spell components.

itemMaterial.name: Yellowwood

effects.note: While wielding a yellowwood longbow or shortbow.

effects.name: Yellowwood Flurry
effects.note: When you take the Attack action with a yellowwood melee weapon, you can use a bonus action to attack again with it. You don't add your ability modifier to that damage unless it is negative.

entries: Found in tropical environments, yellowwood trees grow on hillsides and along rivers and streams. The trees grow tall, reaching above the canopy for light. Due to year-round sun and a wet climate, there are very few rings in the trunks of yellowwood trees. The bark of these trees is dark brown and can be peeled back easily, revealing much lighter wood underneath. The wood of a yellowwood tree is flexible and lightweight. It can be challenging to work with, as it tends to overextend when shaped. Due to yellowwood's density, items made of it are 50 percent lighter than their mundane counterparts.

items: While you're wielding a yellowwood longbow or shortbow, being within 5 feet of a hostile creature doesn't impose disadvantage on your ranged attack rolls.

When you take the Attack action and attack with a melee weapon made of yellowwood, you can use a bonus action to make an additional attack with that weapon. You don't add your ability modifier to the damage of the bonus attack, unless that modifier is negative.

itemMaterial.name: Zog'agi Glass
entries: The ancient Zog'agi learned to turn the sands of the Glittering Desert into glass strong enough for weapons, armor, furniture, and machinery. The Zog'agi Corporation guards the process.

draconicResonance.name: Final Echo
entries: When the item helps reduce a creature to 0 Hit Points, it can preserve one sentence formed from that creature's final thoughts for 24 hours.

draconicResonance.name: Ruinous Release
entries: After a critical hit with the item, or a critical hit against its wearer, creatures other than the user within 5 feet take {@damage 2d6} damage of the source dragon's associated type.

draconicResonance.name: Waking Dread
entries: On a hit, force the target to make a {@dc 15} Wisdom saving throw. On a failure, it is {@condition Frightened} of the user and cannot take Reactions until the end of its next turn.

draconicResonance.name: Unfixed Nature
entries: Before the item deals damage, choose Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, Poison, or Thunder at random. Its damage becomes that type until the end of the turn.

draconicResonance.name: Tainted Wound
entries: A creature hit by the item cannot regain Hit Points until the start of the user's next turn.

draconicResonance.name: Withering Touch
entries: The item deals double damage to nonmagical plants and plant objects. Once per turn, a Plant creature hit by it takes an extra {@damage 1d6} Necrotic damage.

draconicResonance.name: Fractured Sense
entries: On a hit, force the target to make a {@dc 15} Intelligence saving throw. On a failure, it cannot distinguish allies from enemies when making Opportunity Attacks until the end of its next turn.

draconicResonance.name: Hollowing
entries: After the item damages a creature, reduce the next healing that creature receives before the end of its next turn by {@dice 1d8}.

draconicResonance.name: Betrayer's Opening
entries: Once per turn, deal an extra {@damage 1d6} damage when the target is within 5 feet of one of its allies and no ally of the user is within 5 feet of the target.

draconicResonance.name: Interposing Ward
entries: When the user or a creature within 5 feet is hit, the user can take a Reaction to grant that creature +2 AC against the triggering attack, potentially causing it to miss.

draconicResonance.name: First Light
entries: The item sheds bright light in a 10-foot radius on command. The user can end the {@condition Frightened} condition on one creature touched by that light.

draconicResonance.name: Sheltering Warmth
entries: During a Short Rest, up to six creatures resting within 10 feet gain Temporary Hit Points equal to the user's Proficiency Bonus.

draconicResonance.name: Accord
entries: When the user successfully takes the Help action, both creatures gain {@dice 1d6} Temporary Hit Points.

draconicResonance.name: Stand Fast
entries: The user can reroll one failed Strength, Constitution, or Wisdom saving throw, and must use the new result.

draconicResonance.name: Restorative Shelter
entries: When the item restores Hit Points, reroll one healing die that rolled a 1 or a 2.

draconicResonance.name: Unclouded Sight
entries: The user has Advantage on checks to recognize illusions or deliberate visual disguises and can see {@condition Invisible} creatures until the end of their next turn when activated.

draconicResonance.name: Unbound Motion
entries: The user can end the {@condition Grappled} or {@condition Restrained} condition on themself as a Bonus Action.

draconicResonance.name: Higher Reach
entries: After seeing the result of an ability check but before its outcome is declared, the user can add {@dice 1d6} to the roll.
